bodySections.heading: Why timing matters
paragraphs: This dog distemper-parvo plan sequences doses against parvo in under-vaccinated areas, not against a vague “sometime this season” intention for your dog.

Milestone labels on the dog distemper-parvo table (8 weeks; 12 weeks; 16 weeks; Per clinic protocol) are operational deadlines for daycare, boarding, travel, and multi-pet intros — a nearly finished dog distemper-parvo puppy series is still incomplete.

If your household also wrestles with early socialization vs immunity tradeoff or missed mid-series dose, put those constraints on the same calendar thread as the DA2PP / DHPP booster so one reminder system owns the dog distemper-parvo week.

bodySections.heading: If a dose is missed or delayed
paragraphs: Call the clinic with product names and prior dates the day you notice a missed dog distemper-parvo dose; catch-up timing depends on age and gap length for this dog scenario.

Until the dog distemper-parvo series is current again, reduce the exposure pattern that matches parvo in under-vaccinated areas, and do not wait for an annual wellness slot to ask about a dog distemper-parvo make-up dose.
After the visit, enable 7-, 3-, and 1-day nudges for the next DA2PP / DHPP booster due date so the same dog distemper-parvo miss cannot hide inside a shared family calendar.

faqs.question: Is this dog distemper parvo vaccine schedule a prescription?
faqs.answer: No. It is an editorial planning table aligned with common AAHA/AAFP-style windows and facility patterns. Your veterinarian sets the legal and medical plan for the individual dog.

faqs.question: What if we already missed a date on this dog distemper-parvo schedule?
faqs.answer: Contact the clinic for catch-up timing. Bring prior records, limit high-risk exposure tied to parvo in under-vaccinated areas, and reset reminders as soon as the next dog distemper-parvo due date is known.
